\section{Exact dependent-Gaussian dispersion spectrum}
\label{sec:gaussian}

The linearized quotient Gaussian field may be described directly in curvature
space.  For one color, let
\[
 P=d_1d_1^+
\]
be the orthogonal projection of $C^2(K;\R)$ onto $\im d_1$.  At heat scale
$t>0$, the curvature $F$ is centered Gaussian with covariance $tP$; the three
color components are independent copies.  This retains all shared-link and
linearized Bianchi dependence.

For an interior link $\ell$, define its oriented centered curvature
\[
  Y_\ell=C_6O_\ell S_\ell F\in(\R^3)^6,
  \qquad Q_\ell=\norm{Y_\ell}^2.
\]
Its scalar covariance is
\[
  tK_\ell,
  \qquad
  K_\ell=C_6O_\ell S_\ell P S_\ell^\mathsf TO_\ell C_6.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact star spectrum]
\label{thm:gaussian-spectrum}
For each of the eight interior links of the open side-two four-cube,
\[
 \operatorname{spec}(K_\ell)=
 \left\{0,
 \frac{239}{630},\frac{239}{630},
 \frac{33}{70},\frac{33}{70},\frac{33}{70}\right\}.
\]
Consequently, with independent $Z_j\sim\chi^2_3$,
\[
 Q_\ell\ \overset{d}=\ t\left[
 \frac{239}{630}(Z_1+Z_2)
 +\frac{33}{70}(Z_3+Z_4+Z_5)
 \right].
\]
In particular,
\[
 \E Q_\ell=\frac{1369}{210}t.
\]
\end{theorem}

The zero eigenvalue is the discarded common mode.  The remaining eigenvalues
are all strictly below one, quantifying the covariance contraction caused by
the exact curvature constraints.

\begin{corollary}[Determinant Chernoff bound]
For $q>\E Q_\ell$,
\[
 \Prob(Q_\ell\ge q)\le e^{-I_t(q)},
\]
where
\begin{align}
 I_t(q)=\sup_{0<s<35/(33t)}\Bigg\{sq
 &+3\log\left(1-\frac{239}{315}st\right)\\
 &+\frac92\log\left(1-\frac{33}{35}st\right)\Bigg\}.
\end{align}
\end{corollary}

Unlike a product estimate over six plaquettes, this formula uses the full
restricted covariance.  It is exact for the linearized Gaussian model before
the one-dimensional optimization in $s$.
